{{distinguish|Jónsson algebra|Lindenbaum–Tarski algebra}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Jónsson–Tarski algebra''' or '''Cantor algebra''' is an [[algebraic structure]] encoding a [[bijection]] from an [[infinite set]] {{math|1=''X''}} onto the [[Cartesian product|product]] {{math|1=''X''×''X''}}. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Jónsson|first= Bjarni|last2= Tarski|first2= Alfred|author-link= Bjarni Jónsson |author2-link= Alfred Tarski|year=1961|loc=Theorem 5}}.  {{harvs|txt|last=Smirnov|year=1971|authorlink=Dmitrii Matveevich Smirnov}}, named them after [[Georg Cantor]] because of Cantor's [[pairing function]] and Cantor's theorem that an infinite set {{math|1=''X''}} has the same number of elements as {{math|1=''X''×''X''}}. The term ''Cantor algebra'' is also occasionally used to mean the [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]] of all [[clopen subset]]s of the [[Cantor set]], or the Boolean algebra of [[Borel subset]]s of the [[real number|real]]s modulo [[meager set]]s (sometimes called the [[Cohen algebra]]).

The group of [[Order isomorphism|order-preserving automorphisms]] of the [[free object|free]] Jónsson–Tarski algebra on one [[generator (mathematics)|generator]] is the [[Thompson groups|Thompson group]] {{math|1=''F''}}.

==Definition==

A Jónsson–Tarski algebra of type 2 is a set {{math|1=''A''}} with a product {{math|1=''w''}} from {{math|1=''A''×''A''}} to {{math|1=''A''}} and two 'projection' maps {{math|1=''p''<sub>1</sub>}} and {{math|1=''p''<sub>2</sub>}} from {{math|1=''A''}} to {{math|1=''A''}}, satisfying {{math|1=''p''<sub>1</sub>(''w''(''a''<sub>1</sub>,''a''<sub>2</sub>)) = ''a''<sub>1</sub>}}, {{math|1=''p''<sub>2</sub>(''w''(''a''<sub>1</sub>,''a''<sub>2</sub>)) = ''a''<sub>2</sub>}}, and {{math|1=''w''(''p''<sub>1</sub>(''a''),''p''<sub>2</sub>(''a'')) = ''a''}}. The definition for type >&nbsp;2 is similar but with {{math|1=''n''}} projection operators.

==Example==

If {{math|1=''w''}} is any bijection from {{math|1=''A''×''A''}} to {{math|1=''A''}} then it can be extended to a unique Jónsson–Tarski algebra by letting {{math|1=''p''<sub>''i''</sub>(''a'')}} be the projection of {{math|1=''w''<sup>−1</sup>(''a'')}} onto the {{math|1=''i''}}th factor.
